purpose: Heavy Rebuild v2 clean-master architectural and process program for the authoritative municipal incinerator asset, preserving a legible municipal-waste receiving to controlled combustion to flue-gas treatment and residue handling workflow, with operator control, maintenance access, terrain seating, and coherent damage behavior.
ground_program: controlled municipal-service approach with staff entry, waste-hauler access, weigh or inspection control and a road connection appropriate to a civic waste-processing site rather than a generic industrial apron
waste receiving hall or tipping floor visibly precedes combustion; vehicle unloading, bunker or staging space, and feed equipment connect credibly to the furnace line
waste bunker, crane or feed system provides a clear controlled transition from received refuse into the furnace or combustion chamber without dead-end decorative machinery
furnace and boiler hall contains supported primary combustion equipment, refractory or containment volumes, ash-drop or grate relationships, combustion-air systems, and maintenance clearances

energy-recovery equipment, where present, follows the furnace and connects credibly to steam, hot-water, turbine or heat-export equipment without obscuring the incinerator's primary waste-destruction function
flue-gas treatment train follows combustion and includes legible particulate, scrubber, reagent, filtration or equivalent pollution-control stages before the exhaust stack
bottom-ash and fly-ash handling routes remain separated from incoming waste and connect to enclosed collection, quench, transfer, storage or loadout areas appropriate to hazardous residues
control room and operator workspace overlook or directly monitor waste receiving, combustion, emissions treatment and residue systems and contain alarm, records and process-control functions

electrical switchgear, motor-control, reagent storage, water-treatment and backup-power spaces are segregated according to wet, chemical, dust and electrical hazards while retaining credible utility routes
maintenance workshop, parts storage, washdown and service staging provide believable access to cranes, conveyors, furnaces, fans, pumps, filters, ash systems and stack equipment
foundations, trenches, drainage, bunker depths, vehicle grades and stack base seat the facility into terrain without floating machinery, unsupported ducts or a monolithic artificial slab
upper_program: supported galleries and catwalks provide maintenance access to furnace fronts, boiler surfaces, crane rails, ducts, fans, filters, scrubbers and elevated ash or reagent equipment with continuous headroom and guarded edges
any occupied upper control, administration or electrical spaces connect through enclosed supported stairs with usable landings and clear egress
overhead waste cranes or feed machinery have structurally supported rails, bridges and service access consistent with the receiving bunker geometry
flue-gas ducts and process bridges follow supported routes from furnace to treatment stages to induced-draft equipment and stack rather than terminating in open air
the exhaust stack is structurally seated, connected to the final treatment stage and provided with believable inspection or maintenance access
roof zones distinguish receiving hall, furnace/boiler hall, emissions-treatment volumes, service plant and administration while retaining drainage and maintenance access
circulation: waste-hauler circulation forms a one-way or otherwise believable route from site control to unloading and back to exit without crossing principal staff access
operator circulation connects staff entry and control functions to receiving oversight, furnace operations, emissions treatment and ash-handling monitoring points

maintenance circulation reaches cranes, feed systems, furnaces, boilers, fans, filters, scrubbers, reagent systems, ash equipment, electrical rooms and stack base without requiring passage through waste-hauler lanes
hazardous residue and chemical-handling routes remain distinct from ordinary public or staff circulation wherever the site layout permits
every occupied elevated level and process gallery retains a supported route to grade through architectural stairs, with ladders reserved for equipment-only access
damage_constraints: the damaged derivative must remain immediately recognizable as a municipal incinerator through surviving waste-receiving, furnace, flue-gas treatment, ash-handling, control and stack relationships

favor localized bunker fire, furnace breach, boiler or duct failure, ash spill, filter collapse, scrubber leak, electrical fire, corrosion, stack damage and vegetation intrusion over uniform random deletion
major structural breaches must use irregular fracture geometry with gravity-consistent rubble, displaced ducts, failed catwalks or equipment debris below and around the affected zone
damage to a wall, platform, duct, opening or roof must resolve attached glazing, doors, signs, pipes, railings, ladders and fixtures so no floating remnants remain
preserve at least one legible exploration route spanning waste receiving, feed or bunker space, combustion, emissions treatment, control functions and residue handling
damage may disable individual process stages but must not erase the received-waste-to-combustion-to-cleaned-exhaust-and-residue story or reduce the site to a generic factory shell
derive damaged, occupied or contaminated variants only from this immutable clean master

production_admission.note: Authored program is a prerequisite only. Do not add this asset to production-approvals.json until the authoritative v2 automated gate has actually been run and its passing evidence retained.
